classified_spans.label: aligned_response
classified_spans.text: Organizations deploying AI agents must manually select and integrate every layer of the underlying software stack—including foundation models, prompt templates, orchestration frameworks, tool libraries, and runtime environments. Because the AI ecosystem evolves rapidly, with new models, libraries, and optimizations released weekly, engineering teams face a constant treadmill of discovery, compatibility testing, benchmarking, and migration. Each component upgrade risks introducing regressions across interdependent layers, yet delaying upgrades means running on sub-optimal configurations that waste compute, increase latency, or sacrifice accuracy. Current approaches treat the agent stack as static infrastructure, requiring human engineers to manually identify candidate replacements, verify compatibility, run performance evaluations across multiple objectives, and coordinate safe rollouts—a process that is slow, error-prone, and does not scale across fleets of heterogeneous agents. There is no automated mechanism to continuously discover, evaluate, and promote improved stack configurations while preserving full provenance and rollback capability.

TASK: Generate a Problem Statement for a Red Hat patent. 150 words max.

INVENTION IDEA:
---
invention-id: invention-20260716-153029
company: RedHat
created: 2026-07-16T15:30:42
---

# Invention Idea

We propose an autonomous optimization engine that continuously discovers, evaluates, and evolves the complete software stack underpinning an AI agent rather than treating models, prompts, tools, and runtimes as static infrastructure. The system periodically identifies newly available components, automatically assembles compatible execution stacks, evaluates them against organization-specific benchmarks, and compares their performance across multiple objectives such as accuracy, latency, token consumption, and cost. Based on these evaluations, a policy engine promotes superior configurations while maintaining complete provenance explaining every architectural decision and enabling rapid rollback if regressions occur. This creates a self-improving agent platform capable of continuously adapting to the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem without requiring manual engineering intervention.


Output only the problem statement paragraph.
